note: Relationships between canonical risks. 'documented' = a cited source states the link; 'candidate' = proposed by Risk Radar from shared terms or drivers and not yet confirmed by a source. A link is never evidence of causality on its own.

evidence.text: Conflict is the main driver in 12 of the 13 hunger hotspots (June–November 2026 outlook).
Climate shocks, including a possible El Niño bringing drought and flooding, are named drivers.
The Ebola outbreak in eastern DRC could further disrupt markets and humanitarian access.
Middle East escalation or prolonged commodity disruption could push up energy and food prices and trigger financial stress (World Bank, June 2026).
Persistent trade policy uncertainty is listed among downside risks to growth.
World Bank links energy disruption to higher food prices; the link to the specific hunger hotspots is Risk Radar's inference.
Over 80% of phishing emails identified between September 2024 and February 2025 used AI to some extent.
Criminals actively use general-purpose AI in cyberattacks; underground markets sell AI tools that lower the skill needed.
Generative AI makes attacks easier to carry out (CSBN 2025).
Cheaper attack tools, including AI, are one of three drivers of cyber risk to finance (per IMF briefing).
IMF treats cyber threats as a financial stability risk as finance becomes more digital and interconnected; a specific link to non-bank fragility is not established.
Both depend on how AI capabilities and adoption develop; the IMF links valuations to AI investment and profitability, not to AI harms. Shared driver, not cause.
Deepfakes are increasingly used for fraud and scams.
Biological misuse is one of the misuse risks covered in the report; treated here as a sub-risk.
SIPRI warns of heightened risks of miscalculation and escalation as reliance on nuclear weapons grows.
Including 10 conflict-affected countries adds at least 13 million to the out-of-school estimate.
Rising global temperatures and an expected El Niño raise the chance of record heat and shift regional rainfall (wetter Sahel and northern Europe, drier Amazon).
Heat is the most serious climate risk to health in Europe; a sub-risk of extreme weather.
Heat and drought risks to crop production are already critical in southern Europe.
GAR 2025 quantifies disaster costs across all hazards; the share attributable to climate-related extremes is not separated here.
ECDC reports the outbreaks; the role of warming is a widely discussed hypothesis, not stated in this report.
Both sit at the animal–human interface (One Health); a direct link is not claimed by either source.
UN survey respondents rated biorisks and new pandemics as less important than in 2024.
Experts could not rule out meaningful AI uplift for biological weapons.

relations.note: Divergent emphasis rather than a direct contradiction: falling perceived importance of biological threats versus new technical warnings.

evidence.text: Environmental risks slightly declined in perceived importance in the 2026 UN survey.
WMO puts the chance of at least one year above 1.5 °C in 2026–2030 at 91%.

relations.note: Attention versus evidence: perceived importance fell while physical indicators worsened. The WEF also notes environmental concerns are deprioritised in the short term.
